sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Chattanooga, TN?
sections.html:
Chattanooga is the Hamilton County seat on the Tennessee River, and its housing market is split between owners and a large renter base. The Census Bureau counts 52.4 percent of homes as owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024, and the median value of those homes is $283,200. Its July 1, 2025 estimate of 194,144 residents is 6.9 percent above the 2020 base.

The city covers about 142 square miles of land, so conditions change a lot between neighborhoods. Missionary Ridge cuts the city in two several miles east of downtown, Walden's Ridge rises across the river, and the downtown sits at roughly 676 feet. A house on a ridge, in a river-side flood area or in a historic district faces different buyer questions, and your sale plan should start with where the lot sits.

Sellers who want speed usually weigh an as-is cash purchase against a conventional listing. The cash route drops repairs, showings and appraisal conditions. A listing may bring a higher price when the house is in good order and the schedule is flexible.

sections.h2: Which Chattanooga neighborhoods and districts shape resale?
sections.html:
Historic designation can shape what a buyer may do with a house. Ferger Place, Fort Wood and St. Elmo are on the National Register of Historic Places, and the city has local historic districts including Battery Place, Glenwood, Missionary Ridge, M.L. King and Stringer's Ridge. Ask the Land Development Office whether a local district covers your address before you promise a buyer any exterior renovation.

  • Downtown and the North Shore sit near the Tennessee Aquarium, the Walnut Street Bridge and Coolidge Park.
  • St. Elmo and Fort Wood are two of the three National Register neighborhoods, and the M.L. King district runs beside the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga campus.
  • Hixson, Highland Park and Lookout Valley, also called Tiftonia, are separate communities within the city limits.
  • East of Missionary Ridge, Brainerd Road and East Brainerd Road carry traffic toward Hamilton Place.

Public schools fall under Hamilton County Schools, formed in the 1997 merger of the city and county systems. Ask your listing agent or buyer which zone a given address falls in before quoting school information.

sections.h2: Does Chattanooga's weather and terrain affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Yes, mainly through flooding history, tornado risk and heat. The river's largest flood came in 1867, and the Tennessee Valley Authority reservoir system built after 1933 now regulates it; the highest stage since then, about 37 feet, came in 1973. The city also records 52 days a year at or above 90 degrees and more than 52 inches of annual precipitation.

Tornadoes have hit the area too. An EF3 tornado struck southeastern Chattanooga on the night of April 12, 2020. A buyer's inspector will look at roof condition, tree cover and drainage on a Chattanooga house, and a seller who has fixed those items in advance gets a cleaner negotiation.

Hilly lots bring their own checks: retaining walls, driveway grades and foundations on sloped ground. Gather any engineer's letters or receipts for past work so the file is ready when an offer arrives.

sections.h2: How much is Chattanooga property tax and when is it due?
sections.html:
The city rate is $1.93 per $100 of assessed value, set by the City Council, according to the city's tax information page. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value and commercial at 40 percent, so a $283,200 house, the Census median value, has assessed value of $70,800 and a city bill near $1,366. Hamilton County taxes come on top of that figure.

Bills are mailed in September, are due on October 1, and can be paid without penalty through the last day of February. From March 1, interest and penalty total 1.5 percent a month. Delinquent taxes from the prior year are filed in Hamilton County Chancery Court in March, and the page says property can be sold after three years of delinquency.

The City Treasurer can be reached at 423-643-7262 and is located at Room 100, 101 E. 11th Street. Tennessee law does not require a bill to be mailed, so a missing notice does not excuse a late payment. Pull a copy from the city's property tax search before closing.

sections.h2: What can seniors do to freeze Chattanooga city taxes?
sections.html:
Homeowners 65 or older can apply for the city's Tax Freeze, which holds the city portion of the bill steady for one year. The application page sets a combined 2025 income limit of $63,470 and says the home must be the primary residence. The 2026 application deadline is April 5, 2027.

The freeze covers city taxes only. County taxes and fees such as stormwater are not frozen, and the owner has to reapply every year or the taxes revert to the current rate and value. Applicants submit proof of ownership, residency, age and income, and the Senior Programs line is 423-643-7274.

If you plan to sell, keep the application current until closing, since a lapse sends your city bill back to the current rate and value.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Hamilton County value?
sections.html:
Request an informal review from the Hamilton County Assessor of Property first. The county's reappraisal page lists useful proof: sales prices of similar properties in the immediate area within the last three years, a recent private appraisal and photos. The 2026 informal review window is closed, and results are mailed.

Call the Assessor at 423-209-7300, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., to ask about the next cycle. The city's tax page says properties are reappraised every four years and that the County Board of Equalization takes appeals if the informal review does not settle the matter, also at 423-209-7300.

If the county board denies the appeal, the state's appeal guide sets the next filing at August 1 of the tax year or 45 days after the local notice, whichever is later.

sections.h2: Can I run a short-term rental in Chattanooga before selling?
sections.html:
Only with a city certificate, and the zoning rules are tight. The Short-Term Vacation Rental page says every host needs a certificate. A homestay is owner-occupied for at least 183 days a year and costs $250 to apply or renew. An absentee rental costs $500 and is allowed only in commercial zones C-C, C-R, C-MU1 and C-MU2 and form-based zones CC, CX, IX, RF, RV and SH.

Certificates last one year and the Board of Zoning Appeals cannot exceed the 25 percent density cap. Applications have a 60-day life from submission, and a rezoned property cannot get an absentee certificate for 18 months. For a seller, the useful rule is that a valid certificate can be transferred to a new owner of the same address, though the occupancy type cannot change. Call the Land Development Office at 423-643-5891 with questions.

sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded and what does Tennessee charge?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the Hamilton County Register of Deeds, Marc Gravitt, at 400 Courthouse, 625 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, phone 423-209-6560, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office records deeds, powers of attorney, mortgages, plats and military discharges and collects the fees and taxes due.

Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of price, so a $283,200 sale produces about $1,048. The state also lists a $0.115 per $100 mortgage tax on borrowed amounts above the first $2,000. Ask the title company for the full cost list before the closing date.

faqs.q: How long does a Chattanooga cash sale take?
faqs.a: It can close within a couple of weeks when the title is clear and any estate or lien paperwork is ready. The Hamilton County Register of Deeds records the deed after signing. Delays usually come from payoff letters and co-owner signatures, not from the buyer.

faqs.q: What is the Chattanooga city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's tax page lists $1.93 per $100 of assessed value. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value. You also owe Hamilton County tax, so add the county rate from the Trustee at 423-209-7270.

faqs.q: Who pays the Tennessee transfer tax on a Chattanooga sale?
faqs.a: The tax is $0.37 per $100 of price and is collected when the deed is recorded. Check your purchase contract for who is responsible. Your title company will show the amount on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house that has a short-term rental certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. A certificate can transfer to the new owner of the same property if the buyer files the transfer application. It cannot move to a different address, and the occupancy type stays the same.

faqs.q: When is the next Hamilton County reappraisal?
faqs.a: The city's tax page says properties are reappraised every four years. Call the Hamilton County Assessor at 423-209-7300 for the next effective date.
